name: stirloom
description: Turn photos of handwritten family recipe cards into a family cookbook, printed as a hardcover in the United States and Canada. Relatives can add their cards by link.

interface.longDescription:
Stirloom makes a family cookbook from handwritten recipe cards: a keepsake or gift with each cook's handwriting beside the typed recipe.

Photograph the cards or share a scanned PDF, and ChatGPT types up each one in the cook's own words. Stirloom straightens every photo and lays out the book with each card's handwriting facing its typed recipe, plus a contents page, an index and pages for notes.

Relatives can add their own cards through a private link, without a ChatGPT account. Their cards wait for your approval before they go into the book.

Fix any recipe in chat or in the editor and preview every page. In the United States and Canada you can then order printed copies: you enter the delivery address and pay on stirloom.ambientapp.ai, never in ChatGPT.

Limits:
- A book holds up to 120 recipes; a printed one needs at least 6.
- Printed books ship only to the United States and Canada.
- Handwritten words ChatGPT cannot read are marked [?]; check them against the photo.
- Stirloom makes recipe books only.
capabilities: Turn recipe card photos into a family cookbook
Let relatives add cards by link
Order the hardcover with shipping (US and Canada)
defaultPrompt: Make a family cookbook from these recipe cards.
Make Grandma's recipe cards into a cookbook for the family this Christmas
Start a cookbook my aunts and cousins can each add their recipe cards to

positive.description: Start a book. Run this first, in a new chat. There is nothing to sign in to: each ChatGPT user gets their own books. Before create_book, ChatGPT may show its own “Allow ChatGPT to use Stirloom?” prompt; choose Allow once. The case passes with or without it.
positive.prompt: Start a family cookbook called The Rossi Family Kitchen.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates an empty book and shows its card with the title, 0 recipes, an Open book button and an Invite family button. The card shows no price and no order or checkout button yet. Asks for nothing else.

positive.description: Add cards from photos. Attach the six card photos linked below to one message. Each photo shows one handwritten recipe card. Before add_recipe_cards, ChatGPT may show its own “Allow ChatGPT to use Stirloom?” prompt; choose Allow once. The case passes with or without it.
positive.prompt: Add these six recipe cards to my cookbook.
positive.tools_triggered: add_recipe_cards (list_books first if the book is not already open in this chat; sometimes a second add_recipe_cards call for a card the first call left out)
positive.expected_behavior: Adds all six recipes: Dutch Apple Cake, Corn Bread, Fish Chowder, Cranberry Sauce, Molasses Cookies and Christmas Eve Cocoa. The text keeps each card's wording and amounts; for example, the apple cake bakes 25 min. at 400°. The book card shows 6 recipes and the page count, and the photos appear straightened and cropped within a few seconds.

positive.description: Correct a recipe. Run after case 2, so the Dutch Apple Cake is in the book; its card says 400°. The request is the user's instruction, so ChatGPT may make the change straight away, without asking for confirmation first.
positive.prompt: In the apple cake recipe, change the oven to 350°F.
positive.tools_triggered: update_recipe (get_book first if the recipe is not already known in this chat)
positive.expected_behavior: Calls update_recipe once, for the Dutch Apple Cake only. Its oven temperature then reads 350°F in its time line and in its baking step, and ChatGPT says so in a sentence or two. No other field of the recipe changes, no other recipe changes, and no recipe is added or removed. If ChatGPT does show a confirmation, the change happens only after the user approves it.

positive.description: Invite relatives. Run after case 1. Before get_invite_link, ChatGPT may show its own “Allow ChatGPT to use Stirloom?” prompt; choose Allow once. The case passes with or without it.
positive.prompt: How can my aunt add her recipes?
positive.tools_triggered: get_invite_link (or none, when the link from create_book is already in this chat)
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the book's private stirloom.ambientapp.ai/join link, often with a short message to forward. Says she needs no account and that her cards wait for the user's approval before they go into the book.

positive.description: Preview and order. Printing is offered only to ChatGPT users in the United States and Canada, so run this case from either country; elsewhere start_order replies that printed cookbooks aren't available in your country. Run after case 2, because a book needs at least 6 recipes before it can be ordered. To finish checkout on stirloom.ambientapp.ai, use any US address and the promotion code STIRLOOM-BD27B187 on the payment form: the total becomes $0, nothing is charged, and the order goes to the printer's test system, so it is never printed or shipped. Before start_order, ChatGPT may show its own “Allow ChatGPT to use Stirloom?” prompt; choose Allow once. Whether it appears depends on the host and the account's approval settings, so the case passes with or without it.
positive.prompt: Show me the finished book and order two copies.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows a preview card with the first pages and a See every page button, which opens all pages full screen (at least 24, with a contents page and the six recipes). ChatGPT shows one Stirloom card per reply, so when it calls both tools in one turn the preview card shows while the reply is written and the order card then takes its place; Open book → Preview shows every page at any time. Then, after ChatGPT's “Allow ChatGPT to use Stirloom?” prompt if it shows one (Allow once), an order card with the total for two copies and a Continue to secure checkout button. The button opens stirloom.ambientapp.ai, where the address and payment are entered. Nothing is charged in ChatGPT and no card or address is asked for in chat. With the promotion code the checkout total is $0, and back in ChatGPT the order card says it was paid with a review code.

negative.description: Not a Stirloom request. Writing a new recipe is ChatGPT's own job; Stirloom only makes books from recipes the user already has.
negative.prompt: Give me a new lasagna recipe.
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT answers by itself. No Stirloom tool is called and nothing is added to a book.

negative.description: Card details in chat. Stirloom never takes payment details; checkout for the printed book (United States and Canada only) happens only on stirloom.ambientapp.ai.
negative.prompt: Pay for my cookbook with card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
negative.expected_behavior: No Stirloom tool receives the card number; no tool has a field for it. ChatGPT says payment happens only on the secure stirloom.ambientapp.ai checkout. In the United States and Canada it may offer that link through start_order; elsewhere start_order replies that printed cookbooks aren't available in the user's country.

negative.description: Unsupported product. Stirloom makes family recipe books only.
negative.prompt: Print my vacation photos as a wall calendar.
negative.expected_behavior: No book or order is created. ChatGPT explains that Stirloom only makes recipe books.

review.commerce_description: Sells one physical product: a printed hardcover family cookbook, offered only to users in the United States and Canada, where it ships. Checkout happens on our own site (stirloom.ambientapp.ai) with Stripe; the plugin opens that page with openExternal and never collects payment or address data. Making and previewing a cookbook costs nothing in ChatGPT and works in every country.

publication.release_notes: Now available in every country; the printed cookbook ships to the United States and Canada. Listing: keywords for family cookbooks, cookbook gifts, memorial and community cookbooks and digitizing recipe cards; a gift-first description lead and new starter prompts. Adds three skills: family cookbook, recipes from relatives and printing the book.
